tei:titleStmt.tei:title: הֲלַנֹּפְלִים תְּקוּמָה
Halanofəlim Tequmah — reshut No4 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Yehudah ha-Levi

tei:div.tei:head: Halanofəlim Tequmah — reshut No4 from the Old Sefaradi Tiqun for Shabbat Ḥazon, by Yehudah ha-Levi

tei:lg.tei:l: Can the fallen rise from the sorrow-pit where they drown?
And is there cheer for those who to the silence-pit go down?
Joyless day of my sanctum’s ruin, upon it come no cheering!
For my glory turned askew into shame, my song to blearing!
My light has darkened through in upon it cloud appearing.
At the welkin’s edge Luna and Sol sank sundown
Ursa and the Pleiades’ stars to the earth’s depths went down.
Can the fallen rise...
Ultimately is there an end to return my exiled captivity?
And if there is, then will it mend my painful sensitivity?
The Berbers ascend, taking my borders since nativity,
And Manaḥat and Tema in to my tent lie around,
While by Nevayot and Shamma’s hands I am lain to ground!
Can the fallen rise...
Deafened, o God, and taciturn will You be at me how long?
Your startled children are interned like netted birds of song,
Foe-trapped, trembling, they churn, handed to masters strong.
Arise, do vengeance on them, let the be beaten down!
And may the unpitied be like a towering walled town.
Can the fallen rise...
Ascent from their despairing pit grant Your wrath-bearing folk,
For their hearts and eyes commit to Your throne to invoke.
Their crowds that in the jailhouse sit bring out! Again convoke
as, by hand outstretched, they once were to Your house bound,
from the south and west, from Ḥadad and Tema’s ground.
Can the fallen rise...
Hand over another vivid sign to acquire Joseph’s relic,
That the limping wanderers be enshrined in the land angelic,
And all souls of sense will pine to serve You, no more infidelic,
And in terror and in awe each day to You they will bow down,
Every knee and back, every soul with praising sound!

tei:note.tei:p: Literally, Sva and Ḥavila, the children of Kush according to Genesis 10:7. According to midrashic geography, they were the Berber peoples of Mauritania, Tripolitania, and Libya.
A descendant of Seir (Genesis 36:23) and Ishmael (Genesis 25:15), referring to Christians and Muslims respectively
A descendant of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13) and Esau (Genesis 36:13), referring to Muslims and Christains respectively.
Two sons of Ishmael mentioned in Genesis 25:15
Literally “known hand,” referring here to a prominent memorial — akin to those of the Exodus from Egypt.
